title: CLR/164/2017 of SMT. ANUPAMA PRAKASH Vs SHRI SURENDRA SINGH

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No.136 of 2017
Maharaja Manujendra Shah
 .... Revisionist
Versus
Shri Surendra Singh & Others.
 ..... Respondents
With
Civil Revision No.164 of 2017
Smt. Anupama Prakash and another ..Revisionists

Versus
Shri Surendra Singh & Others. ..... Respondents

With
Civil Revision No.167 of 2017
Rajkumar Vigyan Bikram Shah .... Revisionist

Versus
Shri Surendra Singh & Others. ..... Respondents
Mr. Jatinder Kumar Sethi, Mr. Ajay Singh Bisht and Mr. Siddhartha Sah,
Advocates for the revisionists.
Mr. B.C. Pande, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Gopal K. Verma, counsel
for the respondents.
Chronological list of cases referred:
1.Dahiben vs. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali (Gajra) (D) Thr Lrs and Others 2020 SCC Online
SC 562
2.Raghwendra Sharan Singh vs. Ram Prasanna Singh, AIR 2019 SC 1430
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Since the controversies involved in
aforementioned civil revisions are same, therefore, they
are being decided by this common judgment and order.

2
2. All the three civil revisions under Section
115 of Code of Civil Procedure 1908 (hereinafter
referred to as 'the Code') are directed against order
dated 13.09.2017, passed by Civil Judge, (Senior
Division), Dehradun in Original Suit No.112 of 2016,
Surendra Singh and others vs. Maharaja Manujendra
Shah and others, whereby applications (paper no. 28A,
30A & 33A) filed by the defendants/revisionists under
Order VII Rule 11 of the Code has been rejected.
3. Plaintiffs/respondent nos. 1 to 4 instituted
the said suit seeking following reliefs:-
a. That a decree for cancellation of the registered sale deed dated
20.03.2014 by defendant no.1 in favour of defendant no.2 and 3
and registered in the office of Sub-Registrar, Dehradun-III at page
No. 91 to 238, Serial No. 471, Bahi No.1, Jild No. 457, on
20.03.2014 declaring the same to be illegal, void without
jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs, be passed
consequently informing the office of Sub Registrar, Dehradun.
b. That a decree for permanent injunction be passed restraining the
defendants their assigns, servants, officers and agents from
anyhow creating third party rights without settling; the matter
with the plaintiffs.
4. Facts leading to filing of aforesaid civil
revisions are that defendant no.4 (respondent no.7
herein) claiming himself to be the absolute owner of the
suit property known as Doonside Estate (Chandal
Garhi) Mussoorie, Dehradun entered into an agreement
to sell/memorandum of understanding, with the
plaintiff (respondent no. 1 to 4 herein). The plaintiffs
were agreed to purchase the suit property in the year
2008, and paid an earnest amount of Rs.27 lakh
towards part of a sale consideration. The plaintiffs and
defendant no. 4 on account of mutual trust between
them did not feel the need of a written agreement at
that time, but, subsequently a written unregistered
agreement was executed on 09.04.2013 on a stamp

3
paper of Rs.100 and the defendant no.4 acknowledged
the receipt of Rs.27 lakhs from the plaintiff. The
defendant no.4 induced the plaintiffs that he is the
owner of the suit property and suit property is free
from all encumbrances. The total sale consideration
was decided to be paid at Rs. 3 crore and the defendant
no.4 has admitted the receipt of Rs. 27 lakhs from the
plaintiffs towards part of sale consideration.
5. Earlier the defendant no. 1 (revisionist in
CLR No. 136 of 2017) instituted a suit no. 359 of 2011,
titled Maharaja Manujendra Shah vs. State of
Uttarakhand and another for a decree of ejectment and
injunction against the state government. It has been
pleaded in the plaint that plaintiff's grandfather Late
Maharaja Narendra Shah was the ruler of erstwhile
princely State of Tehri Garhwal. The suit property was
the personal property of Late Maharaj Narendra Shah
and was never been the property of erstwhile State of
Tehri Garhwal. After the death of Maharaja Narendra
Shah on 22.09.1950 defendant no.1's father Late
Maharaja Manvendra Shah became the sole successor
of all personal properties, including the suit property.
In said suit defendant no.4 (respondent no.7 herein)
moved an application for his impleadment on 19.07.12
which was dismissed on 20.11.12. The suit filed by the
defendant no.1 i.e. Maharaja Manujendra Shah was
dismissed by the trial court vide its judgment and
decree dated 02.04.2019, in which, it has been held
that defendant no.1 is not the owner of the suit
property. The defendant no.1 though was not the
owner of the suit property, had sold the suit property
to defendant nos.2 & 3 (respondent no. 5 & 6 herein)
through registered sale deed dated 20.03.2014. It is
alleged that the sale deed is a collusive one. The

4
plaintiffs no. 2 to 4 in O.S. No. 112 of 2016 sought a
relief that the sale deed dated 20.03.2014 be declared
as illegal and void. Further, relief has been sought for a
decree of permanent injunction restraining the
defendants their assigns, servants, officers and agents
from anyhow, creating third party rights without
settling the matter with the plaintiffs. Defendants filed
separate applications under Order VII Rule 11 of the
Code. The applications so filed by the defendants were
registered as paper nos. 28A, 30A and 33A. In these
applications, it is stated that no cause of action has
arisen to the plaintiffs to institute the suit against the
defendants. It is further stated that the plaintiffs
themselves have filed a copy of agreement to
sell/memorandum of understanding dated 09.04.2013,
which stipulates that any dispute between the parties
to the agreement shall be referred to the sole arbitrator,
namely, Mr. Vaibhav Jain, Advocate.
6. Plaintiffs filed the objection against
applications under Order VII Rule 11 read with Section
151 of Code being paper no. 38C, 40C & 43C
respectively stating therein that the provisions of
Section 54 of Transfer of Property Act are not
applicable and defendant no.4 has no authority to
make a prayer to send the matter to the Arbitrator. The
plaintiffs have not instituted the suit for specific
performance of contract or for enforcement of
Memorandum of Understanding dated 9.04.2013. It is
further stated that the Sections 17 or 49 of the
Registration Act is not applicable in the matter. It is
further stated that the suit of the plaintiffs is not
barred by section 13, 14 & 17 of the Specific Relief Act.

5
7. In Para 15 of the plaint it is stated that
defendant no.1 is admittedly a stranger to the
agreement to sell dated 09.04.2013, and has no right
to interfere in the privity of the contract. It is further
stated that defendant no. 1 is blowing hot and cold in
the same breath and is called upon to go through the
plaint contentions thoroughly. The suit is not for
enforcement of agreement dated 09.04.2013. The suit
is for cancellation of the sale deed which was not
executed by defendant no.4. In case the arbitration
clause is to be invoked it would be appropriately done
between the parties and the defendant no.1 has no say
in the same. Section 8 of the Arbitration and
Conciliation Act is extracted herein:-
"8. Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an
arbitration agreement.-1 [(1) A judicial authority, before which an
action is brought in a matter which is the subject of an arbitration
agreement shall, if a party to the arbitration agreement or any person
claiming through or under him, so applies not later than the date of
submitting his first statement on the substance of the dispute, then,
notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of the Supreme Court or
any Court, refer the parties to arbitration unless it finds that prima facie
no valid arbitration agreement exists.]
(2) The application referred to in sub-section (1) shall not be
entertained unless it is accompanied by the original arbitration
agreement or a duly certified copy thereof.
[Provided that where the original arbitration agreement or a
certified copy thereof is not available with the party applying for
reference to arbitration under sub-section (1), and the said agreement or
certified copy is retained by the other party to that agreement, then, the
party so applying shall file such application along with a copy of the
arbitration agreement and a petition praying the Court to call upon the
other party to produce the original arbitration agreement or its duly
certified copy before that Court.]
(3) Notwithstanding that an application has been made under
sub-section (1) and that the issue is pending before the judicial
authority, an arbitration may be commenced or continued and an
arbitral award made."

6
8. Having considered the principle of law
contained in the Judgments (supra), the trial court has
arrived to the conclusion and has also recorded the
findings that the plaintiffs had a contract to purchase
the property for an amount of Rs. 3 crore, but
defendant no.4 is in collusion with defendant no.1, 2 &
3, therefore, the suit instituted against the defendant
no. 1, 2 & 3 by defendant no.4 was withdrawn. The
defendant no. 4 has stated in the said suit that he is
the owner of the suit property, which has been sold by
defendant no.1 in favour of defendant no.2 & 3. The
sale deed dated 20.03.2014 has been executed by
defendant no.1 in favour of defendant no.2 & 3. The
trial court has also recorded the findings that cause of
action is a bundle of facts on the basis of which cause
of action to institute the suit can be determined. It was
also held that the plaintiffs have agreed to purchase
the suit property from the defendant no.4 to whom the
defendant no.4 placed that he is the owner of the suit
property, but the defendant no.1 has sold the same
property to defendant no. 2 & 3. It was further held
that as there is a collusion between the defendants, the
sale deed executed by defendant no.1 is illegal and the
plaintiffs have cause of action to institute a suit. With
the finding as above, the trial court rejected the said
applications.
9. Having considered the catena of judgments
the trial court vide impugned order dated 13.09.2017
dismissed the applications paper no. 28A, 30A and 33A
filed by the revisionists. Indisputably, the plaintiffs who
have instituted the said suit against the defendants on
the strength of alleged agreement to sell dated
09.04.2013, have not instituted the suit for specific
performance or for recovery of money against the

7
defendants rather they have instituted the suit for
decree of declaration that the sale deed dated
20.03.2014 executed by defendant no.1 in favour of
defendant nos. 2 & 3 be declared as null and void. The
relief sought for by the plaintiffs is not in regard to the
agreement to sell dated 09.04.2013. Unless the
plaintiffs institute a suit for specific performance for
execution of agreement to sell dated 09.4.2013 instead
of seeking a relief of declaring the sale deed dated
20.03.2014 as null and void, the same could amount
that the relief sought in the plaint has no nexus at all
with the agreement to sell dated 09.04.2013. It seems
that the plaintiffs have filed the vexatious suit without
there being any prayer related to the agreement to sell
dated 09.04.2013.
10. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material brought on record.
11. Learned counsel for the revisionists
vehemently argued that there is no privity of the
contract between the plaintiffs and the defendants and
since there is no contract between the plaintiffs and
defendant no. 1, 2 & 3, the suit filed by the
plaintiffs(respondent nos. 1 to 4 herein) seeking a relief
to institute a suit for cancellation of sale deed dated
20.03.2014, itself is not maintainable and no cause of
action arises.
12. Perusal of the record would depict that the
plaintiffs sought a relief of cancellation of the sale deed
dated 20.03.2014 on the ground that the defendant
no.4 has an agreement to sell/Memorandum of
Understanding in their favour on 09.04.2013 and has
received an amount of Rs. 27 lakh from them.

8
Therefore, they have right to file suit against the
defendants seeking a decree of declaration to declare
the sale deed dated 20.03.2014 null and void. Further
relief of permanent injunction has been sought
restraining the defendants from creating third party
rights without settling the matter with the plaintiffs.
13. Having gone through the averments made in
the plaint itself, it is abundantly clear that there is no
privity of the contract between the plaintiffs and
defendant nos. 1, 2 & 3. The decree of declaration of
the sale deed dated 20.03.2014, which has been
executed by defendant no.1 in favour of defendant no.2
& 3 does not give any cause of action to the plaintiffs to
institute a suit seeking declaration for cancellation of
the sale deed dated 20.03.2014 as neither the plaintiffs
nor the defendant no.4 is the party to the sale deed
dated 20.03.2014. It is settled proposition of law that
the plaintiffs should not be permitted to raise the
vexatious claim.
14. Mr. B.C. Pandey, learned Senior Counsel for
the respondents drew attention of this Court towards a
judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the
case of Dahiben vs. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali
(Gajra) (D) Thr Lrs and Others 2020 SCC Online SC
5621 and contended that the court below had not
considered the provisions contained in Order VII Rule
7. Order VII Rule 7 is extracted herein
7. Relief to be specifically stated- Every plaint shall state
specifically the relief which the plaintiff claims either simply or
in the alternative, and it shall not be necessary to ask for
general or other relief which may always be given as the Court
may think just to the same extend as if it had been asked for.
And the same rule shall apply to any relief claimed by the
defendant in his written statement.

9
15. Having considered the submissions of
learned Senior counsel for the respondents, this Court
is of the view that the learned Senior counsel for the
respondents could not convince this Court that there is
a privity of the contract between the plaintiffs and
defendants no. 1, 2 & 3 in so far the agreement to
sell/memorandum of understanding dated 09.04.2013
is concerned. The plaintiffs may have right to go for
enforcement of their legal rights, if any pursuant to the
agreement to sell/memorandum of understanding
dated 09.04.2013, but the plaintiffs have not sought
any relief pursuant to the memorandum of
understanding dated 09.04.2013, the relief sought by
the plaintiffs in the suit is out of the memorandum of
understanding, dated 09.04.2013 executed between
the plaintiffs and defendant no.4.
16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of
Raghwendra Sharan Singh vs. Ram Prasanna
Singh, AIR 2019 SC 14302, in para 7 has held:-
7. Applying the law laid down by this Court in the
aforesaid decisions on exercise of powers under Order 7 Rule 11 of the
CPC to the facts of the case in hand and the averments in the plaint, we
are of the opinion that both the Courts below have materially erred in
not rejecting the plaint in exercise of powers under Order 7 Rule 11 of
the CPC. It is required to be noted that it is not in dispute that the gift
deed was executed by the original plaintiff himself along with his
brother. The deed of gift was a registered gift deed. The execution of
the gift deed is not disputed by the plaintiff. It is the case of the plaintiff
that the gift deed was a showy deed of gift and therefore the same is not
binding on him. However, it is required to be noted that for
approximately 22 years, neither the plaintiff nor his brother (who died
on 15.12.2002) claimed at any point of time that the gift deed was
showy deed of gift. One of the executants of the gift deed - brother of
the plaintiff during his lifetime never claimed that the gift deed was a
showy deed of gift. It was the appellant herein original defendant who
filed the suit in the year 2001 for partition and the said suit was filed
against his brothers to which the plaintiff was joined as defendant No.

10
10. It appears that the summon of the suit filed by the defendant being
T.S. (Partition) Suit No. 203 of 2001 was served upon the defendant
No.10 plaintiff herein in the year 2001 itself. Despite the same, he
instituted the present suit in the year 2003. Even from the averments in
the plaint, it appears that during these 22 years i.e. the period from
1981 till 2001/2003, the suit property was mortgaged by the appellant
hereinoriginal defendant and the mortgage deed was executed by the
defendant. Therefore, considering the averments in the plaint and the
bundle of facts stated in the plaint, we are of the opinion that by clever
drafting the plaintiff has tried to bring the suit within the period of
limitation which, otherwise, is barred by law of limitation. Therefore,
considering the decisions of this Court in the case of T. Arivandandam
(AIR 1977 SC 2421)(supra) and others, as stated above, and as the suit
is clearly barred by law of limitation, the plaint is required to be
rejected in exercise of powers under Order 7 Rule 11 of the CPC.
17. This court is of the view that it was the duty
of the court to consider as to whether the plaintiffs are
entitled to get the relief sought by them? It has been
held that a vexatious claim should be thrown out at the
threshold.
18. Having considered the ratio of the Hon'ble
Apex Court in Raghwendra Sharan Singh (supra), this
Court is of the view that the plaintiffs though have
instituted the suit for seeking a decree of declaration
for cancellation of the sale deed dated 20.03.2014 as
well as a decree of permanent injunction against the
defendants, who are the true owner of the property, it
is not the case of the plaintiffs that the suit property
belongs to the State Government and the sale deed has
been executed by defendant no.1 in favour of defendant
no. 2 & 3 without any authority of law.
19. It is apt to note here that the plaintiffs have
not instituted the suit in a representative capacity
under Order I Rule 8 of the CPC. What has been

11
argued by learned counsel for the respondents is that
since the defendant no.1 is not the owner of the suit
property as the suit filed by him has already been
dismissed holding that he is not the owner of the suit
property, in such contingencies, the defendant no.1
should not have executed the sale deed.
20. The arguments of learned counsel for the
plaintiffs are that the defendant no.1 is not the owner
of the suit property and had no authority to execute
the sale deed in favour of defendant no. 2 & 3 and the
sale deed executed by him is illegal and void. Learned
counsel for the plaintiffs has argued that the plaintiffs
are entitled to get the decree executed in their favour.
He further submits that though the relief of declaration
of sale deed dated 20.03.2014 has been sought but
having considered the fact that the plaintiffs have paid
an amount of Rs. 27 lakhs to the defendant no.4, the
Court may have modify the relief in view of the
provisions contained in Order VII Rule 7 of the Code.
The submission of learned counsel for the respondents
is misconceived. The relief sought in the plaint has no
nexus with the agreement to sell/memorandum of
understanding dated 09.04.2013. Assuming that the
Court may grant a decree of declaration that the sale
deed dated 20.03.2014 is void, so, no fruitful decree
would be passed in favour of the plaintiffs as such. The
plaintiffs will not be entitled to get a fruitful decree, the
continuation of the proceedings of original suits would
be considered as vexatious claim. The learned trial
court has not considered the application under Order
VII Rule 11 of the CPC, in its right perspective and has
committed illegality in recording the perverse findings
that the cause of action is a bundle of fact, which gives
right to institute a suit to the plaintiffs.

12
21. Having considered the relief sought by the
plaintiffs in their suit and the grounds taken up to
institute the suit and applying the law laid down by
Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid judgments regards
exercise of power under Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC,
this Court is of the view that the plaintiffs who have
not instituted the suit based on the agreement to
sell/memorandum dated 09.04.2013 are not entitled
for the relief claimed in the suit. The trial court has
committed illegality in dismissing the applications filed
by the defendants. The trial court has committed
illegality in dismissing the applications filed under
Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC. The order passed by the
trial court is unsustainable in the eyes of law. The
same is liable to be set aside. The same is set aside.
The applications, being paper no. 28A, 30A and 33A,
filed under Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC are allowed.
All the revisions are accordingly allowed. The suit filed
by the plaintiffs/respondents is hereby dismissed.
22. No order as to costs.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
